summary: Read-only evidence from Supabase project gcctapykhrdyxikieemn, taken at 2026-10-21 23:57 to 2026-10-22 00:00 UTC (33 queries, all in production-evidence.md). Brief section 2.9 is accurate on every number it gives: 124 minute ticks since 13:40 UTC with 0 errors, run 6305e565 read 7 of 9 feeds into 64 candidates (45 held, 12 new, 3 rejected, 4 selected) for $0.002243, 3 photos stored, 4 briefs for 22 October (3 single-image, 2 without a picture), and 0 accounts, tokens, jobs, revisions and publications. The production state adds five things the brief does not say: (1) all four 22 October briefs will lapse at 05:30, 10:00, 14:30 and 17:30 UTC because no @dneskai account row exists, and the two non-news briefs with 14-day expiry are thrown away with them instead of moving to a later slot; (2) generation's 43 s minimum start leaves only 5 s for collection, media and briefs, and the pending-brief recheck alone already takes a median 2.7 s, so 5 of 45 ticks with pending briefs would have deferred a generation job; (3) every run is reported partial because the deliberately disabled Instagram stages count as incomplete; (4) 10 cron runs (12:50-13:35 UTC) produced no tick row and their HTTP answers are gone after about 6 h, so a rejected tick is invisible; (5) only 1 of 3 stored pictures can fill a slide, and both OpenAI candidates got 403 on the page fetch. Input is thin by measurement: the longest of 64 texts is 261 characters, 20 of 64 candidates (Hacker News) have no text at all, and no candidate has 3 or more pictures. The retention prune function and cron job are missing (documented as an owner item); the first daily tick at 02:18 UTC had not run yet, so its retention error is still a prediction. Migration history shares one version with the repository out of 25 production entries since 13 October.

With briefs pending the median of those steps is 4.1 s and 5 of 45 ticks exceeded 5 s; on collection nights every tick 20:00-20:15 exceeded it. When jobs exist, those ticks defer generation by 5 minutes (tick-budget-exhausted).

findings.recommendation: Run generation first when a queued job exists (it is the one category with a hard 43 s need), or give it a dedicated tick; make the pending-brief recheck cheap (production-04). Add a tick-level counter of generation deferrals to the Costs tab.

impact.reason: Good stories held for a missing date never reach the owner and held rows accumulate.

findings.recommendation: Give the owner a 'held' list with release/discard in the Zdroje tab, and add held candidates to the daily retention (for example 14 days).

truth.evidence: V3: run 6305e565 held 45 of 64; 5 held for collection-source-date-unavailable-or-stale at 0.88-0.96; run edc97cf7 70 held. Code: the selection pool only takes status='new' (events_briefs.sql:106-108) and :158 sets held for stale dates; no route or function moves held back to new (grep of src and migrations for candidate status updates: only Jev classification inside a run and finish). No retention for candidates found.

findings.title: A collection no-op took 16-19 s because two database reads run before the hour check
findings.claim: At 17:00 and 18:55 UTC (19:00 and 20:55 Prague) the collection step returned collection-not-due after 19,379 and 16,080 ms. The precheck calls yieldToPublication() and runs() before the cheap pragueHour < 22 test.

evidence.excerpt: const list = await runs(), today = pragueMarketingDate(clock());

impact.statement: Such a stall pushes the generation step past its 5 s window (production-03) for that tick; the cause (cold start or slow database) is not established.
impact.reason: Occasional 16-19 s stalls eat the tick; a reordering is trivial but the cause is unproven.

findings.recommendation: Test the hour first (keep the running-run check for after 22:00 and for a running run that started earlier), and log per-call timings for the two reads to find the stall.

truth.evidence: scheduler.ts:260-267: intakePaused, yieldToPublication (:261) and runs() (:262) run before the hour test (:267); lines correct. Q7 durations 19 379 / 16 080 ms re-read from evidence; cause (cold start vs slow DB) not established, as the claim says.

findings.title: Jev reserves about 10x its real cost and the collection ceiling is far from binding
findings.claim: Each Jev batch reserves $0.003 and costs $0.000193-0.000366; the night spent $0.002243 against $0.024 reserved, and both runs together $0.019456 against $0.208. Jev costs about $0.000035 per candidate.

impact.statement: Jev costs about $0.07 a month at one night a day (estimate); the $0.25 daily ceiling is only relevant once Apify is on. Inputs for the cost model, not a defect.
impact.reason: A cost-model input with no action (Jev costs about $0.07 a month and ceilings are owner-locked); belongs in the cost map, not the owner list.

findings.recommendation: Use these measured numbers in the cost model; leave the ceiling unchanged (owner rule).

truth.evidence: V4: 8 Jev batches reserved $0.003 each, cost $0.000193-0.000366 (8-16x); run 6305e565 cost $0.002243; all stages reserved $0.208 vs cost $0.019456. Per-candidate $0.000035 = 0.002243/64.

findings.title: Two feeds hit the 20-item cap; three sources have never succeeded
findings.claim: hn-frontpage and techcrunch-ai ended partial with collection-source-item-cap at 20 items. arxiv-cs-ai and arxiv-cs-lg (21 Oct) and github-ai-releases, simonw, rest-of-world (13 Oct) have last_success_at null. meta-ai succeeded with 0 items.

evidence.excerpt: arxiv-cs-ai, arxiv-cs-lg, github-ai-releases, simonw, rest-of-world last_success_at null; meta-ai ok 0 items

impact.statement: TechCrunch is the source of 1 of 4 picks and 7 of 12 unselected strong items; its cap may drop more. Five sources contribute nothing yet.
impact.reason: Five silent sources and capped feeds shrink the candidate pool; mostly follow-up checks already planned.

findings.recommendation: Check the arXiv fix on 28 Oct and github-ai-releases on 23 Oct as NEEDED.md plans; consider raising techcrunch-ai's cap and lowering HN's (production-05).

truth.evidence: V4: hn-frontpage and techcrunch-ai partial collection-source-item-cap (20 items) confirmed; meta-ai ok with 0 items confirmed. Title says 'three sources have never succeeded' but the claim lists five feeds with last_success_at null (arxiv-cs-ai, arxiv-cs-lg, github-ai-releases, simonw, rest-of-world), plus Instagram profiles never collected (activeprogrammer held provider-http-400-invalid-input, evolving.ai and robotic held).
truth.correctedClaim: Two feeds hit the 20-item cap; five feeds (arxiv-cs-ai, arxiv-cs-lg, github-ai-releases, simonw, rest-of-world) have never succeeded, and meta-ai returned 0 items.
